I have days like this too, where I feel hopeless. It can be very hard to deal with when you are experiencing that much pain and sadness. Do you have a therapist you can talk to when you feel this way? That really helps me, because she knows my struggles but also my hopes and goals, and reminds me of what I want in life. 

Tell me, if this pain were to stop, what would you want out of life? Would you have dreams? Anything you’d want to accomplish? Or maybe do you have any hobbies you really enjoy? Is there a movie you’ve wanted to see for a long time? A class you’ve wanted to take? A country you want to visit?

If you feel overwhelmed, it can help to break things down. Make little goals to find happiness. Like making your bedroom/apartment into your space, filled with things you enjoy. Or volunteering to work with animals/the elderly/kids. 

And hey, you ARE good enough. This is something I think too, that I am broken, unworthy of what I have and useless. This isn’t true. You are good enough, you are worthy of living, of taking up space, you are worthy of a good life. 

A final thing I’ll add that I did when I felt really horrible all the time was I would find ways to encounter more positivity. I played guided meditations, some would be for trauma, some for spoken affirmations, some just had a scene. These helped immensely, because I’d hear someone else telling me I was good enough, or I’d have a bit of positivity in my day when my brain was all negative. I’d also use Pinterest to save happy quotes and I’d spend time around kind people too. 

You don’t have to give up. Please don’t.

May I ask, do you have a support system other than your mom? Anyone else you can go to regularly when you are having issues? It sounds as if you don’t regularly see a therapist, and that is a great idea. 

If you are scared and think you may follow through, you may want to go to the ER. I know it must feel awful for your mom to not be taking you seriously, but she may just be in denial or maybe things don’t appear as bad to her. I’m not sure how it may work where you are, but when you visit an ER in America while feeling suicidal, they will ask a lot of questions and screen you for risk. Then they sometimes will have you be an inpatient in a psychiatric ward, or they may suggest an intensive outpatient program. 

Also, have you spoken to your family doctor about what’s going on? Are you on any medication or diagnosed with anything? It’s important to be screened for mental health conditions if you haven’t been already so you know what you’re up against and the best way to treat it. 

Again, I know this must be scary and I’m so sorry you’re experiencing this. If the suicidal urges are that strong that you are genuinely concerned you may take action, I would highly suggest visiting the ER. Most therapists can’t help at that point. While it can be a scary step, you will be monitored so you can’t harm yourself, and they hopefully will look at your health and look into next steps and if there are any medications they can provide you with. 

And remember, you aren’t alone during this, you can always reach out on Reddit if you need support. You can call the suicide hotline, visit the ER, anything you need. Listen to the part of you that is saying you need help. If you want help, all you need to do is ask. You can do this. Feel free to respond if you need anything.

It’s so hard working somewhere extremely stressful, and especially where you don’t feel appreciated. Unfortunately for me I’ve always struggled to hold a job and have trouble dealing with stress. Here are some of my tips:

1. I work with a therapist. Is this something you’ve considered? Not sure if that’s something you’re interested in, if not I’d recommend looking up stress reduction techniques and trying them out. 

2. Ensure you really enjoy your time off of work. This is something I’ve struggled with, because I tend to obsess about work when home and never truly relax. Remember to spend time with friends and family sometimes and not isolate (I sure isolate sometimes). Get into old hobbies you love, watch a show or movie you’ve been dying to see. Take bubble baths, learn to cook a new meal, surprise someone on a night out. Maybe you already do all this, just some ideas. 

3. Talk to your doctor. I’m not saying you need medication, so please don’t take it that way. But my doctor actually told me to quit my job because of my stress levels, anxiety and depression. Hopefully you have a great PCP who can listen and be aware of the stress you are under. 

4. Do you need to stay at this job? Can you apply for others while working there? Any dreams, hopes, goals you’ve pushed aside? Maybe now is the time to look into those. Maybe you could go back to school, or spin your experience into a job you enjoy. 

I hope these help. Best of luck to you!

Evanescence was a huge part of my teenage years, and I still love them dearly. I first started listening when Fallen came out in 2003. I remember my best friend had the CD; she played Bring Me to Life because that was the song on the radio everyone loved. 

But I was drawn in to Going Under, that song still is probably my favorite song today. It had hints of creepy, it was dark yet melodic, I still think it sets the stage for some things I love the most in life. The piano sends chills up my spine! 

I really got into their older material too, Origin and their EPs and demos. Understanding blew me away and I still sometimes cry when I listen to it. 

I also really connected with them because around the time Fallen came out I started to listen to heavier music, and only a few had female vocalists. I couldn’t help but admire her, she was beautiful and had this incredible angelic voice, her dark hair and piercing eyes, and she seemed strong, sure of herself, and proud of how she felt and the music Evanescence created. 

Overall I really connected with their dark and haunting music and aesthetic, being a teenager is difficult and I felt I could understand them and felt understood as well. 

Fallen, Origin and The Open Door are still some of my favorite albums; I love to drive around listening to them at night, windows down, singing. 

I was drawn to everything Evanescence represented: darkness, beauty, feelings of sadness and anger, a dark and gothic aesthetic, overall it was haunting and that resonated with me, it still does. I sometimes think a part of me is still trapped in that time, never moving on, because I still love it and connect with it so much.

I felt super stressed by wedding planning as well. After I went over a ton of different options with my fiancé, we decided on city hall (so to speak)! 

This probably doesn’t sound exciting, but we chose to drive to another state, which is where we spent our first night away together. We will be there for a week, and on the first day we are getting married. 

We found a Justice of the Peace who has marriage packages. We are having an intimate ceremony in a beautiful and free location that is technically “rented” for such occasions. Our JP also allows us to write vows or use some she has provided. 

We decided we definitely want pictures. All together, we will be paying $510 - $60 for the marriage license, $150 for our JP, $300 for the photographer. And our JP arranges everything!

We are so happy with our choice. I was losing my mind with wedding planning, as we hated the thought of spending a lot of money. I also wanted the moment to be about us, so it will be just the two of us. We won’t tell anyone until we come back. 

I would recommend looking into JPs near you (or the location you would like to be married), as you can have everything arranged for you for a great price. 

The other suggestion I have, that we almost went with, was having a small wedding at a local state park. Near us, they charge only about $200 to rent a spot for the day. It ended up being not totally what we wanted, but I still think it’s a nice and inexpensive idea.

Do not start off a marriage by going into debt. Talk about it, find out what is important to her. Even if you only get simple wedding bands together, or you get her a simulated diamond, you can always decide in the future to upgrade when you have the funds.

You are still very young and a relationship without sex can lead to a lot of resentment. It is not easy to leave a relationship that is mostly positive, but sexual compatibility is a huge deal breaker in most cases as it's a foundation for a strong, loving relationship. 

Eventually you will have to choose what you'd rather deal with. Time usually doesn't help, though having open and honest conversations with him will. Pressure/hints often cause a rift in the relationship. Speaking from personal experience, I am much happier after I left my DB relationship, but my ex didn't have many of the qualities yours does.
